thread.title: Tech Today: AMD's Window of Opportunity, Spotify's Churn, Defending AMAT

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: AMD's Window of Opportunity, Spotify's Churn, Defending AMAT
text:
Square Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Square catching up with Venmo It's payment pioneer versus payment pioneer!
Square 's ( SQ ) personal payments tech, " Square Cash ," is "surging," according to Instinet's Dan Dolev, based on his observations of downloads of the Cash app for mobiles.
And the downloads are "growing faster than Venmo ," the personal payments app of PayPal Holdings ( PYPL ), writes Dolev, and are "nearly on par with Venmo," at 28 million cumulative downloads thus far, just 1 million less than Venmo's.
Despite having a Buy rating on Square shares, Dolev cautions not to focus on just the downloads: "While app downloads are important, they are not the only yardstick as they do not capture usage or monetization.
"E.g. in December, SQ Cash had ~7mn monthly active users, or ~35% of the cumulative downloads."
Square shares are up $1 cents, or 1.8%, at $55.65, while PayPal is down 14 cents at $77.65.
Spotify vs. the free Shares of recently public streaming-music pioneers Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) are up $1.29, or 0.8%, at $160, after Wells Fargo 's Peter Stabler today initiated coverage of the stock with a Market Perform rating and a $150 price target. He appreciates the brand awareness of Spotify-of U.S. consumers surveyed, 42% know the Spotify name "unaided," he relates, which is second only to Pandora Media ( P ), at 54%.
And there's strong "product satisfaction" with Spotify.
"However, our survey work indicated that free products suffice for many users, with Spotify Free users, lapsed Spotify users, and those who have never tried Spotify all self-reporting limited interest in upgrading to Spotify Premium."
That points to Spotify's high, high churn , writes Stabler: "We estimate that in'16-'17, SPOT experienced ~66MM user churn events. While many of these users have been subsequently won back, we believe there are likely tens of millions of prior Premium users who now occupy-and are satisfied with-Spotify's Ad-Supported tier."
Tiernan Ray for Barron's AMD's window of opportunity vs. Intel Shares of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) are up 33 cents, or 2.7%, at $12.78, after Susquehanna Financial 's Christopher Rolland this morning raised his rating on the shares to Neutral from Negative, writing that Intel 's (INTC) delay of its 10-nanometer chip production, announced back on Intel's Q1 call in April, leaves more of an opportunity for AMD to compete on a level playing field.
"AMD is expecting to sample 7nm Zen 2 products at the end of the year," writes Rolland. "For the first time in memory, AMD will compete at a similar process technology as Intel, a strong multi-year tailwind."
Rolland also notes that an ethereum crypto mining chip that was supposed to be big competition -from Chinese chip designer Bitmain -has suddenly surged in price , offering less competition for AMD:
"Initial specs for the $800 E3 rig offered a >3x improvement over premium GPUs. However, in the weeks following, Bitmain discretely increased prices to $2,150 (memory costs?), cutting price/performance by two-thirds... a non-starter."
Micron steady as it goes Micron Technology (MU) continues to get more approving nods this morning: Vijay Rakesh with Mizuho reiterates a Buy rating and a $70 price target, writing that prices of both NAND flash chips and DRAM "remain relatively stable despite a weak first-half build season in PCs, China handsets, and iPhones.
"While seeing some modest declines, we have not seen the significant pricing declines we were expecting entering the year, and we believe pricing will remain a near-term tailwind."
He says Samsung Electronics' ( 005930.Korea ) investments in DRAM manufacturing are nothing to worry about.
Remember, Micron is hosting its annual analyst day meeting this coming Monday. The stock today is up $2.52, or 4.7%, at $56.53.
Bully for Apple, Qualcomm Canaccord Genuity 's Mike Walkley today pounds the table for both Apple (AAPL) and Qualcomm (QCOM), reiterating Buy ratings on the stocks as the worst of their smartphone malaise abates .
For Apple, Walkley notes a survey he conducted that shows "iPhone maintained its leading market share at all 4 major US carriers and overall iPhone sales remained resilient with likely over 50% share at these carriers."
As for Qualcomm, its stock is depressed because investors have "priced in a low probability" of the company getting approval by China for its bid for NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) and resolving its licensing disputes with Apple and one other unnamed customer.
"However, we view the shares as attractive," he writes, "given the potential for strong long-term earnings potential.
"We believe Qualcomm can achieve management targets for $5.25 in F2019 non-GAAP EPS with or without NXP and excluding settling licensing disputes with Apple and Huawei."
Qualcomm stock today is up 63 cents, or 1%, at $56.27.
Buy the smartphone suppliers Speaking of Apple and iPhone , KeyBanc 's John Vinh writes that his surveys of telcos in North America and Europe reveal that days of inventory for the iPhone went "slightly lower" recently, which he takes as an "encouraging" sign.
But demand for Samsung's " Galaxy S9 " smartphone, its flagship device and its main weapon against the iPhone, "has been extremely disappointing ," writes Vinh, "due to a higher price point (~$60 higher at launch) and lack of incremental features compared to previous generation GS8."
Despite "excessive GS9 inventories," which are "concerning," Vinh concludes that investors should be looking to own suppliers of both giants going into the second half. That includes Broadcom (AVGO), Skyworks Solutions (SWKS), and Synaptics (SYNA).
Defending Applied Materials Another party affected by that smartphone slump is chip equipment maker Applied Materials (AMAT), with the Street concerned about the part of Applied's business that makes tools to make large pieces of glass for TV and smartphone displays . Weaker smartphone sales are hurting the business of making organic-light-emitting diode, or OLED , screens at Applied's customers.
But Stifel Nicolaus ' Patrick Ho today steps in to reiterate his Buy rating on Applied shares, and his $71 price target.
"We clearly acknowledge that there is likely to be a decline in total OLED equipment spending in 2018, led by Samsung's projected decline," writes Ho, referring to Samsung's production of displays-the only source at the moment for OLED displays. "However, we remind investors that Applied's display business is not tied only to OLED capacity spending."
People are forgetting, writes Ho, "Applied's dominant or leadership position in the traditional LCD market, as this segment is transitioning to Gen 10.5/11 panel sizes." Several projects, he thinks, will lead to "new tool buys through at least 2020 and perhaps all the way through to 2021."
Applied shares today are up $1.31, or 2.5%, at $55.40.
AT&T's doing better than you think AT&T 's (T) story is better than people realize, writes Wells Fargo 's Jennifer Fritzsche , after traveling yesterday with CFO John Stephens . One worry, of course, is the ongoing prosecution of its bid to acquire Time Warner (TWX), but Fritzsche thinks matters are "moving in the right direction."
The ruling in the government's case against AT&T and Time Warner is coming on June 12 , she notes, and there's a five-day appeals period if necessary, which to her means " we could see the deal close as early as June 18."
The other big worry is where AT&T's video business stands in a world of streaming . AT&T has four different approaches to video, and the one that's not yet here is "a thin client premium over-the-top " offering that "will have the same content as DirecTV but will be a streaming device with a better digital user interface."
That thin client approach, expected to come at the end of the year, will have a much lower "subscriber acquisition cost " for AT&T, notes Fritzsche, and therefore will be priced lower to subscribers, on the order of $80 to $90 per month, $15 to $20 cheaper than DirecTV. The sum of all these efforts "should allow the company a path to generate more revenue from these additional customer services."
AT&T shares today are up 5 cents at $32.13.
